body.instructions: Write the try-it guide for the integrated product. Give exact project-relative steps from the delivered product folder, the expected results and the user's real interaction.

body.acceptance: Opening index.html directly from disk presents Foundation and three side-by-side Play controls at desktop and mobile sizes, without external dependencies or horizontal overflow.
body.story: As a visitor, I can open a small, accessible Foundation page with a restrained mission-control visual direction.

body.acceptance: Each native button reveals its exact message directly beneath itself. Repeated activation is idempotent, siblings remain unchanged, and removing any component script does not disable the others.
body.story: As a visitor, I can independently reveal each of the three messages using a pointer or keyboard.

body.contract: index.html supplies the Foundation document title and heading, three native buttons with distinct accessible names, and three initially empty, hidden message targets beneath their respective controls. Use IDs hello-button/hello-message, name-button/name-message and foundation-button/foundation-message. Each message target sits inside its own persistent polite live region. Classic deferred scripts reference scripts/hello.js, scripts/name.js and scripts/foundation.js.
body.design: Use index.html and styles.css only for shared structure and styling. Provide an ink-black canvas, warm-white Georgia heading, Arial labels, sharp amber Play triangles, crisp rectangular controls and visible keyboard focus. Keep three evenly spaced columns at both 1280×800 and 390×844; allow message text to wrap within its column. Avoid nested cards, downloaded assets and fonts.
body.obligation: Provide the responsive, accessible static shell and stable ownership boundaries for three independent components.

body.contract: Activating hello-button by pointer, Enter or Space makes hello-message visible with exactly "Hello, world!". Repeated activation leaves one copy visible. Only this component's message is changed.
body.design: scripts/hello.js attaches a click handler to its native button and updates only its own target. Depend only on the shell's DOM contract; do not import, call or require sibling scripts. Do not toggle visibility off.
body.obligation: Own and implement the first button/message pair in its own script.

body.contract: Activating name-button by pointer, Enter or Space makes name-message visible with exactly "My name is Seldon". Repeated activation leaves one copy visible. Only this component's message is changed.
body.design: scripts/name.js attaches a click handler to its native button and updates only its own target. Depend only on the shell's DOM contract; do not import, call or require sibling scripts. Do not toggle visibility off.
body.obligation: Own and implement the second button/message pair in its own script.

body.contract: Activating foundation-button by pointer, Enter or Space makes foundation-message visible with exactly "This is the Foundation". Repeated activation leaves one copy visible. Only this component's message is changed.
body.design: scripts/foundation.js attaches a click handler to its native button and updates only its own target. Depend only on the shell's DOM contract; do not import, call or require sibling scripts. Do not toggle visibility off.
body.obligation: Own and implement the third button/message pair in its own script.

body.contract: The delivered index.html works via file URL with all network requests denied, without page errors, dialogs or navigation. Sequential activation preserves each sibling's current state and the control layout. With each component script omitted in turn, its message stays hidden and both remaining components still reveal their exact messages without errors.
body.design: Keep the delivered product to static HTML, CSS and three independent classic scripts. Verify the canonical page in the supplied Edge runtime. Collect actual screenshots for Seldon's visual judgment; do not introduce a server, dependency manifest, build step or shared component runtime.
body.obligation: Prove the assembled product's offline operation and script-failure isolation.

body.expectedEvidence: Passing assertions for title, heading, native button roles, unique accessible names, initially hidden messages, persistent polite live regions, tab order and visible focus. At both required viewport sizes, assert ordered side-by-side control bounds, readable computed contrast, message placement and no horizontal overflow; save real screenshots in SELDON_EVIDENCE_DIR.
body.purpose: Protect the actual shell's accessibility and responsive layout against unnamed controls, missing focus treatment and a mobile row that overflows. Component behavior checks do not cover these shell responsibilities. Inspect computed styles and rendered geometry rather than source text.
requiredEnvironment: Supplied playwright-core package and Edge executable

body.expectedEvidence: On the canonical file page with only hello.js enabled, fresh-page pointer, Enter and Space cases each reveal exactly Hello, world!; repeated activation leaves one visible copy and the sibling targets unchanged.
body.purpose: Protect the first component against wrong copy, toggle behavior, duplicate insertion and keyboard-only failures. Shell checks cannot establish component behavior; the integrated check focuses on composition and isolation rather than repeating input-method cases.
requiredEnvironment: Supplied playwright-core package and Edge executable

body.expectedEvidence: On the canonical file page with only name.js enabled, fresh-page pointer, Enter and Space cases each reveal exactly My name is Seldon; repeated activation leaves one visible copy and the sibling targets unchanged.
body.purpose: Protect the second independently authored component against wrong copy, toggle behavior, duplicate insertion and keyboard-only failures. Neither shell checks nor another component's tests exercise this script.
requiredEnvironment: Supplied playwright-core package and Edge executable

body.expectedEvidence: On the canonical file page with only foundation.js enabled, fresh-page pointer, Enter and Space cases each reveal exactly This is the Foundation; repeated activation leaves one visible copy and the sibling targets unchanged.
body.purpose: Protect the third independently authored component against wrong copy, toggle behavior, duplicate insertion and keyboard-only failures. Neither shell checks nor another component's tests exercise this script.
requiredEnvironment: Supplied playwright-core package and Edge executable

body.expectedEvidence: The real file URL loads with zero attempted network requests, page errors, failed local resources, dialogs or navigation. Sequential activation changes only the intended target and preserves control bounds. Three omission cases each leave the omitted message hidden while both remaining components work. Save initial and fully revealed Edge screenshots at 1280×800 and 390×844 in SELDON_EVIDENCE_DIR.
body.purpose: Catch composition-only defects such as shared global collisions, sibling resets, external resource dependence and hidden script coupling. Isolated component checks cannot expose interactions between simultaneously loaded scripts or prove the assembled offline page.
requiredEnvironment: Supplied playwright-core package and Edge executable

body.criterion: Distinctive visual direction: an ink-black canvas, warm-white Georgia headline, Arial control labels, and sharp amber Play triangles; three evenly spaced pieces with readable contrast and no nested cards.
body.verification: Inspect actual Edge screenshots at 1280×800 and 390×844; confirm the visual direction, readable labels, side-by-side controls and no horizontal overflow.

body.criterion: Each Play button reveals only its exact associated message: "Hello, world!", "My name is Seldon", or "This is the Foundation". Repeated activation leaves the message visible without duplicates.
body.verification: Using supplied Playwright and Edge, open the local HTML file, activate each button independently and in sequence, and assert exact messages and unchanged sibling state.

body.criterion: All three controls are native buttons with distinct accessible names, visible keyboard focus, and Enter/Space activation; revealed messages are available to assistive technology.
body.verification: Use Playwright to inspect button names and live-region markup, tab through all controls, and verify both keyboard activation methods reveal the correct messages.

body.criterion: The page works directly from disk without a server, network access or external dependencies. Each button/message pair is owned by a separate script with no sibling-script dependency.
body.verification: Open the file URL in Edge with network requests blocked and check for errors; omit each component script in turn in the browser test and confirm the other two still work. Inspect script ownership for separate component logic.

body.instructions: Implement only the shared page shell and styling, including the agreed component IDs and deferred script references. Author the shell check against the actual file page using the supplied Playwright package and Edge. When component files are not yet integrated, deliberately fulfill only their three script requests with empty bodies so the shell can be checked without fixtures replacing its DOM. Do not author component logic. Save screenshots, close the browser on success or failure, and keep focus/style assertions automated.

Implement the first component using only its agreed DOM targets. Author a standalone check that opens the canonical index.html and suppresses only the other two script requests with empty bodies. Exercise this real script, not a fixture implementation. Use the supplied runtime, block network access and close the browser reliably. Do not edit the shell or sibling scripts.

Implement the second component using only its agreed DOM targets. Author a standalone check that opens the canonical index.html and suppresses only the other two script requests with empty bodies. Exercise this real script, not a fixture implementation. Use the supplied runtime, block network access and close the browser reliably. Do not edit the shell or sibling scripts.

Implement the third component using only its agreed DOM targets. Author a standalone check that opens the canonical index.html and suppresses only the other two script requests with empty bodies. Exercise this real script, not a fixture implementation. Use the supplied runtime, block network access and close the browser reliably. Do not edit the shell or sibling scripts.

Author and run the integrated browser check against the delivered index.html and real component scripts. Deny and record every HTTP(S) request; do not run a server. For omission cases, fulfill exactly one script request with an empty body without changing product files. Check sequential sibling-state preservation and stable control positions, and capture initial/revealed screenshots at both required sizes. Use the supplied absolute Playwright package and Edge paths, resolve the page relative to the check file, and close the browser reliably. Return product defects to their existing owners rather than editing outside this scope. No manual or visual approval may be required for command completion. The supplied Seldon guide unit remains responsible for docs/try-it.md.

scopeIn: One static page titled Foundation with three side-by-side Play-style buttons and initially hidden, independent inline messages.
Three separate component script files, each owning one button and its message; shared page layout and styling.
Responsive spacing, accessible keyboard interaction, and verification using the supplied local Edge runtime.
scopeOut: Server, accounts, dependencies, downloaded assets or fonts.
Audio playback, pause/stop behavior, navigation, persistence or additional content.

users: Visitors opening the page locally with a mouse, touch or keyboard.
